rows.evidence: Q1: section 'Deficit irrigation in fruit trees and vines', Fig. 10 and Table 1 <U+2014> the authors report their own long-term peach experiment near Cordoba comparing RDI, SDI and full irrigation (stem water potential, yield, fruit volume in the fourth year, 2005); Fig. 7/8 also fit the authors' own sunflower data to a harvest-index model.
rows.notes: The paper is predominantly a review of deficit irrigation (own data are limited to one peach experiment and re-analysed sunflower data). It contains no evidence on digital or app-based scheduling systems combining crop-stage, weather and soil-moisture information. Its own result shows that, for the same applied water, RDI (deficits concentrated outside rapid fruit growth) maintained yield and fruit size in peach whereas SDI reduced them by about 10-15%; the principle that deficits should be timed to avoid sensitive stages is derived from this and from cited literature, not from any scheduling technology. Q1 is borderline because the paper is a review article; if treated strictly as a review Q1 would be 'no', which does not change the remaining answers.

notes: Full text appears complete. Review-type paper with a small embedded primary dataset (peach RDI/SDI experiment, Cordoba). No evaluation of digital/app scheduling tools anywhere in the paper.
